name: RavenDB
tagline: ACID document database for .NET and beyond, with auto-indexing, Corax search and multi-master replication.
description: RavenDB is a C# document database built around fully ACID transactions on JSON documents and an indexing engine that creates indexes automatically from the queries you run. Its own Corax engine (or Lucene) handles full-text search, and map-reduce indexes give materialized aggregates. The 7.x line added vector search and AI integrations, and 7.2 is the current LTS (7.2.7 shipped in October 2026). Clusters use multi-master replication with Raft for cluster-wide operations, and sharding has been built in since 6.0. It is especially popular with .NET teams who want an opinionated, batteries-included database with a strong management Studio.

pricing.notes: Free Community licence (renewed yearly, must run the latest major); Professional and Enterprise subscriptions; RavenDB Cloud is billed per instance.

scale.notes: Multi-master replication across nodes and data centers; native sharding since 6.0.

strengths: ACID transactions across documents on a single node, plus cluster-wide transactions
Automatic indexes created from query patterns, with no manual index design for simple cases
Built-in full-text, spatial and vector search
Map-reduce indexes act as always-up-to-date materialized aggregates
Document revisions allow reverting a database to a point in time
Excellent .NET client and a polished web Studio
weaknesses: Smaller community and talent pool than MongoDB
AGPL or paid licences; the free Community licence has feature and version limits
Indexes are eventually consistent with writes by default
Many features skew towards .NET; other clients are thinner
useCases: Embedded databases in desktop or edge applications
notIdealFor: Teams outside the .NET ecosystem needing broad tooling
